title: Full Training Intensity Cleared
description: Sleep duration, HRV, and resting heart rate all look at or above your personal baseline — a positive, multi-signal confirmation that today is a reasonable day for planned HIIT or max-effort training, with no recovery-based reason to downgrade intensity.
source: Huberman Lab (training/recovery balance); product heuristic (trigger combination)

conditional.question: Sleep, HRV, and resting heart rate all look good today — want confirmation you're clear for planned hard training?

actions.details: No intensity downgrade is indicated by recovery signals today. This is a confirmation nudge, not a new action — proceed with whatever intensity was already planned.

benefits: Prevents over-cautious training downgrades when recovery signals are genuinely good
Builds trust in the trigger system by surfacing positive signal, not only warnings
Reinforces that intensity decisions are being made on real data, not guesswork
science: The absence of any negative deviation across three independently-measured recovery signals (sleep duration, HRV, resting heart rate all at or better than personal baseline) is the inverse of the multi-signal recovery-deficit pattern, and is used here only as a confirmation signal rather than to drive any new behavior.
contraindications: Not a substitute for subjective readiness (soreness, motivation, life stress) — a good ring reading does not override how the person actually feels
Does not account for local/muscle-group recovery (e.g. DOMS from a prior session) — Oura's whole-body signals cannot and should not be used to infer local muscle recovery status

learning_resources.title: Foundations of Fitness: Structuring Workouts Optimally — Huberman Lab

evidence_metadata.scientific_rationale: Three-signal AND requiring sleep duration >= 95% baseline, HRV >= 100% baseline, and resting HR <= 100% baseline, one night — the mirror image of the recovery-deficit/delay-hard-training pattern, used purely as a 'no downgrade needed' confirmation rather than a call to increase training beyond what was already planned.

evidence_for_protocol.notes: There is no direct Huberman Lab claim being surfaced here beyond 'if recovery signals are good, there's no recovery-based reason to hold back' — this protocol exists to counterbalance over-suppression risk (brief section on conflict rules) rather than to add a new scientific recommendation.

evidence_for_trigger.notes: The 95%/100%/100% thresholds are an unvalidated, symmetric-ish mirror of the caution/delay tiers' downside thresholds, chosen so this only fires on genuinely strong across-the-board nights, not merely 'not bad' ones.

expected_effect.short_term: No physiological effect intended — informational only, meant to reduce unnecessary training downgrades.
expected_effect.long_term: If this under- or over-fires in practice, tune thresholds against real trigger co-occurrence and user feedback once outcome tracking exists.
